tn_records.note: Grk προαίρεσις ἐλευθέρα (“free deliberate choice”). Or “free choice.”
Grk εἱμαρμένην…ἀπαράβατον; Justin’s ironic redefinition of “fate” as the fixed outcome of choice.
Grk ἐλευθερία τῆς προαιρέσεως. Or “freedom of choice.”

tn_records.phrase: the one who wants to can
tn_records.note: Grk ὁ βουλόμενος δύναται (“the one who wills is able”).

tn_records.phrase: of his own decision and of his own power
tn_records.note: Lat. liberum et sui arbitrii et suae potestatis — free decision / free choice of one’s own judgment and power.
Grk αὐτεξούσιον…τουτέστιν ἐλεύθερον (“self-determining, that is, free”).

tn_records.phrase: yet a slave to whatever he wills to serve
tn_records.note: Grk δουλεύοντα…ᾧ βούλεται; free, yet a slave to what he wills to serve.
Grk ὡς ὀφειλήν (“as what is due / owed”). Or “as his due.”
Irenaeus’s image: the clay must stay soft under the Craftsman’s hand.
Baptism follows persuaded faith and a willing new life, not coercion.
